scams.name: Seminyak Money Changer Sleight-of-Hand on Jalan Kayu Aya / Legian Corridor
scams.description: Seminyak is ground zero for Bali's most-documented tourist-money scam — the money-changer sleight-of-hand on the Jalan Kayu Aya and Legian corridors. The 2025 scam pattern: (a) kiosks advertising 'No Commission, Best Rate — AUD 1 = Rp 10,400' when Bank Indonesia mid-rate is Rp 10,100 (2–4% padded); the displayed rate lures tourists in, but the real fraud is the sleight-of-hand short-counting during hand-over — a stack labelled Rp 2M becomes Rp 1.6M–1.7M in the tourist's hand; (b) 'big note trick' where the teller stacks bills with large-denomination notes on the outside but smaller-denomination filler inside; (c) 'no wait for recount' pressure where the teller physically moves the cash away into a drawer before the tourist can recount; (d) 'commission fee' surprise at transaction end; (e) street-corner 'private exchange' with 'better rate' offered 100m off Jalan Kayu Aya (100% scam). For older travellers: (1) exchange ONLY at PT Central Kuta Money Changer or BMC (Bali Maspintjinra) — both have verified Google 4.7+ reviews and multiple Seminyak/Kuta branches; published daily rates on window; security camera visible; (2) count bills yourself IN FRONT of the teller THREE TIMES before leaving — this is the anti-sleight-of-hand defence; (3) compare rate to Bank Indonesia mid-rate (bi.go.id) daily — refuse rates more than 2% below; (4) AVOID every 'no commission, best rate' kiosk with hand-written signs; AVOID every street-corner 'private exchange' offer; (5) for large amounts (US$500+), go to a Bank BCA or Bank Mandiri branch during business hours — slightly worse rate but zero risk; (6) pay with credit card at shops/restaurants for chargeback protection; (7) community reports from 2025 confirm the pattern persists; (8) if short-counted, demand the security video review or call Polsek Seminyak (+62 361 755 398).
scams.avoidance: Exchange ONLY at PT Central Kuta or BMC (4.7+ Google, published rates) Count bills yourself THREE TIMES IN FRONT of teller before leaving Refuse rates more than 2% below Bank Indonesia mid-rate (bi.go.id) AVOID all 'no commission, best rate' kiosks and street-corner offers For large amounts, use Bank BCA or Mandiri branch — zero risk
scams.location: Jalan Kayu Aya (Eat Street) money changer kiosks, Jalan Legian strip exchangers, Jalan Camplung Tanduk side-street booths, hotel-lobby rate-padding

scams.name: Seminyak Beach Club Drink Spiking at Finns / Atlas / Potato Head
scams.description: Seminyak and adjacent Canggu have Bali's densest beach-club scene — Finns, Atlas, Potato Head, La Brisa, Ku De Ta — and host a documented 2025 organised drink-spiking pattern targeting solo female travellers and groups of international tourists. Community reports warn of organised drink-spiking at Finns Beach Club specifically, and the South Korean Embassy has issued a 2025 warning about serious crimes in Bali. The 2025 scam pattern: (a) organised crews of 2–3 people approach solo or small-group female tourists offering free drinks; (b) drink delivered already-spiked (benzodiazepines, ketamine, or GHB); (c) victim experiences rapid disorientation within 20–40 minutes; (d) perpetrators 'help' the victim leave the venue and rob/assault; (e) some reported cases involve theft of credit cards with sessions opened after leaving. Other linked scams: (f) 'VIP table' hosts at Finns / Atlas charging Rp 3M–15M for bottles; (g) 'bottle service required for entry after 10 PM' (untrue); (h) 'friendly local' offering to share 'private villa party' (high-risk follow-up). Community reviews of Finns, Atlas, and Potato Head cover the venue-specific landscape. For older travellers and especially female travellers: (1) ALWAYS order bottled/sealed drinks ONLY, watch the bartender open them, and NEVER leave your drink unattended — go to the bathroom WITH your drink or abandon it; (2) refuse ALL free drinks from strangers — the 2025 pattern is unambiguous; (3) refuse 'VIP table' hosts pushing bottle service; (4) travel in groups of 2+ minimum; if solo, inform your hotel of your whereabouts and a return-by time; (5) if you feel disoriented, go DIRECTLY to the venue security (not a 'friendly helper') — all beach clubs have security teams and can sit you in the office until a trusted contact arrives; (6) Bali Tourist Police hotline: +62 361 759 687 (24/7); (7) South Korean Embassy 2025 warnings about serious crimes in Bali are embassy-level — take seriously; (8) for older couples, Potato Head during DAY hours (11 AM–4 PM) is family-friendly and low-risk; the spiking pattern peaks 9 PM–2 AM; (9) keep emergency contacts in your phone lock-screen.
scams.avoidance: ALWAYS order sealed/bottled drinks; watch bartender open them NEVER leave drink unattended; go to bathroom WITH drink or abandon REFUSE all free drinks from strangers Travel in 2+ groups; inform hotel of return-by time if solo Bali Tourist Police 24/7: +62 361 759 687
scams.location: Finns Beach Club Canggu/Seminyak, Atlas Beach Club Canggu, Potato Head Beach Club Seminyak, La Brisa Canggu, Ku De Ta, private beachfront VIP zones

scams.name: Seminyak Villa Rental Fake-Listing & Booking-Platform Fraud
scams.description: Seminyak is Bali's densest private-villa rental market — hundreds of listings on Airbnb, Booking.com, Agoda, and on less-regulated platforms. This creates a 2025 fake-listing ecosystem. Community reports repeatedly warn against unverified listings, especially on Facebook groups, and document the current villa-scam landscape. The 2025 scams: (a) fake Airbnb listings using stolen photos from legitimate luxury villas at 30–50% below-market price — 'too good to be true' with urgent 'must book today' pressure; (b) WhatsApp-only dealers requesting 50–100% advance payment via bank transfer (non-refundable); (c) Facebook Marketplace 'Bali Villas' groups with fake profiles — properties don't exist or are already occupied; (d) 'villa management' scams where a middleman sub-rents a real villa without owner permission; (e) on-arrival bait-and-switch where the villa is 30% smaller, in a different neighbourhood, or noisier than photos; (f) deposit-refusal fraud where the 'cleaning deposit Rp 2M' never returns. For older travellers: (1) book ONLY via Booking.com, Agoda, or Airbnb (verified property, guest-protection guarantee, refund policy) — NEVER Facebook groups, Instagram DMs, or WhatsApp-only sellers; (2) cross-reference the villa name + photos on Google Maps + Tripadvisor before booking — if the villa name has zero Google results, it's a scam; (3) pay via the booking platform's secure payment (Airbnb pays only AFTER check-in); NEVER bank-transfer to a private WhatsApp number; (4) refuse 'urgent discount must book today' pressure; (5) for luxury villas, use reputable management companies: The Ungasan, Villas of Bali, Elite Havens — direct bookings with verifiable office addresses; (6) on arrival, photograph EVERYTHING (existing damage, cleanliness, inventory) to avoid fake cleaning-deposit charges; (7) community reports document current 2025 villa-market issues; (8) for groups, book 2 nights first then extend if satisfied — don't lock in long stays blindly.
scams.avoidance: Book ONLY via Booking.com, Agoda, or Airbnb (verified + guest protection) Cross-reference villa name + photos on Google Maps + Tripadvisor NEVER bank-transfer to private WhatsApp; use platform secure payment For luxury, use reputable management: Ungasan, Villas of Bali, Elite Havens Photograph villa condition on arrival to avoid fake cleaning-deposit charges
scams.location: Airbnb/Booking.com Seminyak villa listings, Facebook Marketplace 'Bali Villas' groups, WhatsApp-only private-rental dealers, Seminyak villa management companies

scams.name: Seminyak Beauty Salon 'Add-On Service' Overcharge & Card-Fraud Scam
scams.description: Seminyak's beauty salon ecosystem — nail, hair, spa, facial — has exploded 2023–2025 to serve the international-tourist market, and a 2025 add-on-service overcharge scam with credit-card fraud overlay has emerged at the high end. One 2025 traveler reported a US$2,500 fraud case at a Seminyak salon. The 2025 scam pattern: (a) tourist agrees to 'Rp 350K mani-pedi' package; (b) during service, staff 'discover' skin/nail 'issues' and upsell: 'fungal treatment Rp 500K, gel extension Rp 400K, hand massage Rp 200K, paraffin treatment Rp 300K' — bill balloons to Rp 2M–5M (US$125–$320); (c) customer refuses, staff brings 'manager' who claims payment was 'agreed verbally'; (d) critically, some salons then clone the credit card during payment — staff takes card out of sight, swipes through skimmer, runs fraud transactions US$500–$3,000 days later; (e) a specific US$2,500 fraud case has documented this clone pattern; (f) high-end hair salons running similar upsell patterns on 'keratin treatment extension' from Rp 800K quote to Rp 4M charged. For older travellers: (1) book ONLY at Google 4.7+ salons with 100+ reviews — reputable: Cozy Nail Bali, The Nail Boutique, Amo Spa, Bodyworks Spa; (2) CONFIRM the package price IN WRITING (photograph the menu) BEFORE any service starts; (3) REFUSE every 'add-on' upsell during service — say firmly 'tidak terima kasih, lanjutkan saja' (no thanks, continue) to any in-service upsell; (4) NEVER let the credit card leave your sight — tap-to-pay at the reception or follow the staff to the terminal; (5) use ONE dedicated travel debit card with low daily limit (Rp 3M) and transaction alerts; (6) for larger treatments (keratin, colour, facial), pay cash only; credit-card cloning risk is real per community reports; (7) if in-service pressure escalates, leave — you have the right to walk out; (8) if defrauded, file complaint at Polsek Seminyak (+62 361 755 398) for credit-card chargeback documentation; (9) report any salon-card fraud to the Indonesian Consumer Protection Agency (YLKI).
scams.avoidance: Book ONLY at Google 4.7+ salons (Cozy Nail, The Nail Boutique, Amo Spa) Confirm package price IN WRITING; photograph menu BEFORE service REFUSE every 'add-on' upsell mid-service (say 'lanjutkan saja') NEVER let credit card leave your sight; tap-to-pay at reception For large treatments (keratin/colour), pay cash only — cloning risk real
scams.location: Jalan Kayu Aya beauty salons, Jalan Oberoi nail/spa clusters, Jalan Raya Seminyak hair-salons, Jalan Laksmana Eat Street adjacent spas

scams.name: Seminyak Tailor 'Custom Suit' Bait-and-Switch Fraud
scams.description: Bali's custom-tailoring tourism (suits, dresses, shirts) has been a Seminyak staple for 20+ years — but quality and pricing variance in 2025 has created a bait-and-switch scam at the lower end. Community reports document the tailor landscape and provide guidance on reputable operators. The 2025 scams: (a) 'special suit Rp 2.5M in 24 hours' offered by street-front tailors — delivered suit uses cheap polyester (not promised wool/cashmere), wrong measurements, and poor stitching; the '24-hour promise' is a red flag for low-quality rush jobs; (b) hotel-concierge kickback tailors at 2x fair prices (Rp 6M for a suit that reputable shops charge Rp 3.5M); (c) 'deposit 50% only Rp 1.5M' for a suit the shop never actually makes; (d) 'cashmere Italian wool' claimed but actually polyester-blend — the customer can't verify until home; (e) final fitting 'extra alteration Rp 500K' for alterations that should be included; (f) 'shipping to your hotel' surcharge Rp 300K when shop-pickup is included; (g) counterfeit 'designer fabric' (Tom Ford, Zegna labels on non-branded fabric). For older travellers wanting a custom suit: (1) budget Rp 3.5M–6M (US$220–$380) for a REAL quality 2-piece suit with good wool (not polyester) — Rp 2M 'deals' are polyester; (2) book ONLY at reputable long-established tailors with Google 4.6+ and 50+ reviews: Mr Ho's Tailor (Kuta/Seminyak), Sabina Tailor (Seminyak), Stephen's Tailor (Legian) — verify multi-year presence; (3) allow MINIMUM 5 days for a proper suit (multiple fittings); refuse '24-hour' and '3-day' promises; (4) insist on SEEING the fabric bolt, feeling it, and confirming content percentage in writing (e.g., '100% Australian merino wool Super 120s'); reputable shops post certification; (5) write the measurements down yourself after each fitting; require the tailor to redo alterations if wrong (included in original price); (6) pay 30% deposit, 70% on final satisfied fitting — NEVER 100% upfront; (7) if hotel concierge recommends, check independent Google reviews — some hotel tailors are kickback scams; (8) counterfeit designer fabric: if it costs Rp 3M, it's not authentic Tom Ford wool (Tom Ford fabric alone is US$300+ per metre); (9) buy from your home tailor if you want guaranteed quality; Bali tailors are variable.
scams.avoidance: Budget Rp 3.5M–6M for real quality wool 2-piece; avoid Rp 2M deals Book at reputable long-established tailors: Mr Ho's, Sabina, Stephen's Allow 5+ days, multiple fittings; refuse '24-hour' promises Insist on SEEING fabric bolt + content percentage in writing Pay 30% deposit, 70% on satisfied fitting — NEVER 100% upfront
scams.location: Jalan Legian tailor clusters, Jalan Raya Seminyak custom-suit shops, Jalan Oberoi tailor row, hotel-concierge-referred tailors

scams.name: Seminyak Massage/Spa 'Extended Service' Pressure & Card-Fraud Overlay
scams.description: Seminyak's spa and massage ecosystem runs from legitimate hotel spas (Bodyworks, The Amala, Amo Spa, Kush at The Yoga Barn) to a 2025 pressure-upsell scam cluster on the smaller side-street venues. This is distinct from the Ubud pushy-massage pattern (see Ubud) in that Seminyak adds a credit-card fraud overlay — one 2025 case specifically documented US$2,500 in cloned-card fraud at a Seminyak salon. The 2025 scams: (a) tourist agrees to 'Balinese massage Rp 250K, 60 min' at a side-street spa; (b) during service, 'extra essential oils Rp 150K, hot stones Rp 200K, extended service Rp 300K' pushed continuously; (c) at the end, bill Rp 1.2M–2.5M (US$75–$160) with 'manager' claiming pre-agreed; (d) Seminyak-specific overlay: card cloning via out-of-sight swipe — fraud charges appear days later at Rp 3M–15M; (e) 'special extended pampering package Rp 750K' upsold verbally during booking but not written on receipt; (f) 'couples ritual Rp 2M upgrade' from standard couples massage. For older travellers: (1) use ONLY hotel spas (Bodyworks Seminyak, Amo Spa, Kush at Yoga Barn, The Amala) OR Google 4.7+ spas with 100+ reviews (Jari Menari, Blu Stone Spa); (2) CONFIRM the total price IN WRITING BEFORE entering the treatment room; photograph the menu; (3) REFUSE every 'extra essential oil, extended service, hot stone' upsell mid-treatment — firmly say 'lanjutkan saja, tidak perlu tambahan' (continue, no extras needed); (4) NEVER let your credit card leave your sight — tap-to-pay at reception; if card goes out of sight, call your bank to alert for potential cloning; (5) for couples packages, confirm price for BOTH people in writing; beware 'upgrade to ritual Rp 2M' mid-treatment; (6) treatments should be Rp 250K–600K for standard Balinese/aromatherapy at reputable spots; anything claimed to be 'Rp 150K discount' is quality-compromise or scam-pattern; (7) tip 10–15% in cash at end — legitimate spas don't add auto-gratuity to credit card; (8) pay cash when possible to eliminate card-cloning risk entirely.
scams.avoidance: Use hotel spas (Bodyworks, Amo, The Amala) OR 4.7+/100+ review spas CONFIRM total price IN WRITING; photograph menu BEFORE entering room REFUSE all mid-treatment upsells ('lanjutkan saja, tidak perlu tambahan') Tap-to-pay at reception; NEVER let card leave your sight Pay cash for high-risk salon/spa — eliminates card-cloning
scams.location: Jalan Kayu Aya spa cluster, Jalan Oberoi massage parlours, Jalan Laksmana side-street spas, Jalan Raya Seminyak sunset-lounge adjoining spas
